title: Circuit Symbols and Diagrams
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Circuit Symbols Worksheets (Cells, Lamps, Switches, Buzzers, Motors)
standard_text: Use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on circuit symbols and diagrams: cells, batteries, lamps, switches, buzzers and motors, reading and describing circuit diagrams. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Symbols make circuits easy to read.
key_sub: Cell, lamp, switch, buzzer, motor: one shape each, joined by straight wires.
body_html:
How to think about it

Circuit diagrams use recognised symbols so everyone can read them.

  • Cell: long thin line (+) and short thick line. Battery: two or more cells joined.
  • Lamp: circle with a cross. Buzzer: half circle. Motor: circle with M. Switch: open (gap) or closed.
  • Wires are straight lines. Current flows only around a complete loop.
Example

A circle with a cross inside?

Symbol for a light

Answer: a lamp

Example

Open switch in the loop: does current flow?

There is a gap

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Drawing a lamp as a plain circle.
  • Counting the two lines of one cell as two cells.
  • Thinking an open switch lets current flow.

faq.q: Why do we use circuit symbols?
faq.a: They are quicker to draw than pictures and every scientist and electrician recognises them, whatever language they speak.

faq.q: What is the symbol for a cell?
faq.a: A long thin line (the positive side) and a short thick line next to it. Two or more cells joined make a battery.

faq.q: How do you show a switch?
faq.a: An open switch is drawn with the line lifted away from the contact, leaving a gap. A closed switch is drawn as a line joining the two dots.
